meta.title: Integrator windup and anti-windup strategies
meta.tools: PI loop with actuator saturation on a first-order plant; clamping and back-calculation anti-windup
meta.summary: Show how a saturated actuator lets a PI integrator 'wind up' and cause large overshoot, predict the extra overshoot from the integrated error during saturation, and compare conditional integration and back-calculation fixes.
meta.problem: When the actuator hits its limit the controller keeps integrating an error it can't act on. How bad is it, and which fix works best?
meta.theory:
Plant G = 1/(s + 1) (τ = 1 s, gain 1), PI K_p = 5, K_i = 5, actuator limited to ±1.2 (just above the 1.0 needed at steady state). During saturation the
integrator accumulates ∫e dt; after leaving saturation it must be 'unwound' by an equal area of negative error, so overshoot area ≈ excess
integral. Back-calculation feeds (u_sat − u) back into the integrator with gain 1/T_t, T_t ≈ √(T_i·T_d) or ≈ T_i.
meta.method:
Unit step at t = 0, 10 ms steps. Variants: no anti-windup, conditional integration (freeze when saturated and error drives further), back-calculation
(T_t = 0.2 s). Measured overshoot, settling, and the negative-error area after saturation vs the integral accumulated during it.

rows.quantity: No anti-windup: overshoot area ≈ error integrated beyond the linear integrator state
rows.note: integral of (1 − y) accumulated while saturated
